items.title: Why the last tactical mile is crucial to acquisition reform
items.author: Dr. Katherine A. McGrady
items.summary: If acquisition reform is to succeed, it must migrate to the warfighter's last tactical mile, the president and chief executive officer of CNA writes.
items.body:
The Pentagon is right to treat acquisition reform as a warfighting imperative. In an era when technology is evolving fast, and our adversaries have built arsenals designed to compete asymmetrically, those who can adapt at speed will win.

The effort to implement the Warfighting Acquisition System — transforming the acquisition system around speed, accountability and mission relevance — is both necessary and overdue.

However, if this reform is to deliver its full promise, it must extend beyond headquarters processes, portfolio structures and contracting authorities. Acquisition reform needs to migrate to the last tactical mile — where warfighters confront real-world friction, adapt in real time and generate operational lessons that should shape requirements, accelerate integration and compress acquisition timelines.

The true test of these reforms will not be how quickly decisions move through the system, but how effectively the system learns from the edge, where combat effectiveness is ultimately determined. The avenue to more certain victory leads to and from the warfighter, embracing analysis at the last tactical mile.

America’s warfighters operate at the edge, just as good operations analysts — like those in my own organization — must do in a fast-moving acquisition ecosystem. Successful acquisition reform will need insights from the edge, empowered by empirically trained analysts (uniformed and civilian) who understand systems, tactics, strategy and operations as seen from the perspective of the sailor, soldier, airman, guardian or Marine.

Speed in acquisition will not be achieved by process reform alone. Analysis at the tactical edge is often overlooked but in need of energy and capital to capture insights that drive decisions. Rapid acquisition to field systems that provide military utility demands a continuous learning loop between those who build capability and those who employ it under actual operating conditions — and the ability to measure results quickly.

In this loop, field-level insights should not be treated as downstream feedback after system deployment; they must become upstream drivers of requirements refinement, system integration and prioritization.

By institutionalizing this feedback loop, the department can reduce costly redesign cycles, shorten decision timelines and field capabilities that are not only delivered faster but have greater military value. This is consistent with the department’s own shift toward “speed of relevance,” operational outcomes, and fulfilling the promise to the warfighter.

The department does not need to build this learning architecture from scratch. Proven models already exist in pockets within the force. The Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory, for example, works closely with warfighters to test and analyze new systems. The operator perspective gets fused early into the technical development process, which then allows fielding at speed. This approach to development can outpace program-of-record development, even when going after the same warfighting gaps.

But this warfighter-centric approach should not be confined to formal military innovation organizations alone. Operator-informed analysis must extend across the defense ecosystem, accelerating integration, reducing acquisition timelines and scaling trusted results.

This is not mere assertion. When acquisition works, whether rapid or otherwise, it does so in part because analysts got in the foxhole, in the aircraft, or inside the combat information center to assess, validate and inform acquisition efforts from the point of view of the warfighter.

I know, because my analysts have led that kind of impactful work. We have designed and executed tests of prototypes in the real world, providing independent technical analysis of performance. Analysis at the tactical edge has uncovered critical problems that have to be addressed before warfighters can safely use systems. It has also revealed new tactical use cases for systems — ones that weren’t anticipated by the manufacturer.

The complexity of the counter-IED fight in Operations Iraqi Freedom and Enduring Freedom offers a clear case where warfighter feedback alone was not enough to assess a technology’s utility. So many counter-IED systems were being pushed to the warfighters that it became important to understand which systems worked under which conditions.

Yet one of the most challenging problems in analysis is proving a negative. In other words, if an IED did not go off, was that because of the counter-IED system or not? Our analysts deployed alongside Marine Corps units to collect data and employed complex statistical methods to make that determination. Lives were at stake, and our analyses made a difference.

The department’s shift to the Warfighting Acquisition System is both necessary and timely. Victory on future battlefields belongs to the nation that can create military advantage through rapid acquisition and wartime adaptation. That much is clear. But enduring speed does not come from process redesign alone. It comes from building an acquisition enterprise that learns from the warfighter — where data is analog and results require deep insight to interpret.

If the department fully integrates such a learning loop, it will do more than shorten timelines. It will create a force that adapts faster, integrates better and delivers combat-relevant capability at the pace warfare demands. This is how acquisition reform becomes warfighting advantage.

Dr. Katherine A. McGrady is the president and chief executive officer of CNA, which operates the Center for Naval Analyses, a federally funded research and development center that pioneered the field of operations analysis in support of the U.S. Navy during World War II.
items.titleZh: 为何“最后战术一英里”对采办改革至关重要
items.summaryZh: CNA总裁兼首席执行官写道，采办改革若要取得成功，就必须下沉到作战人员的“最后战术一英里”。
items.zhFull:
五角大楼将采办改革视为作战的当务之急，这是正确的。在技术快速演进、对手已建成旨在实施非对称竞争的武库的时代，谁能快速适应，谁就能取胜。

实施“作战采办系统”——围绕速度、问责和任务相关性来改造采办体系——既必要，也来得太迟。

然而，这项改革若要充分兑现其承诺，就必须超越总部流程、投资组合结构和合同授权等范畴。采办改革需要向最后一战术英里延伸——在那里，作战人员面对真实世界的摩擦，实时调整适应，并产生本应塑造需求、加速集成、压缩采办周期的作战经验教训。

检验这些改革的真正标准，不是决策在体系中流转的速度有多快，而是体系从作战末梢——战斗力最终在此决定——学习的成效有多高。通往更确定胜利的道路通向作战人员，又从作战人员出发，其中包含对最后一战术英里的分析。

美国的作战人员在最前沿行动，正如优秀的作战分析人员——比如我所在机构的同行——必须在一个快速变化的采办生态系统中做到的那样。成功的采办改革需要来自前沿的洞见，由经过实证训练的分析人员（军职和文职）赋能，他们能从水兵、士兵、空军官兵、太空军官兵或海军陆战队员的视角理解系统、战术、战略和作战。

采办速度仅靠流程改革无法实现。战术前沿的分析常常被忽视，却需要投入精力和资本，以捕捉驱动决策的洞见。快速采办并交付具有军事效用的系统，要求能力建设者与在实际作战条件下使用能力者之间形成持续的学习回路——并具备快速衡量结果的能力。

在这一回路中，来自战场层面的洞见不应被视为系统部署后的下游反馈；它们必须成为需求细化、系统集成和优先级排序的上游驱动因素。

通过将这一反馈回路制度化，国防部可以减少代价高昂的重新设计循环，缩短决策时间，并交付不仅更快到位、而且具有更大军事价值的能力。这与国防部自身转向“以相关性为速度”、注重作战成效以及履行对作战人员承诺的方向是一致的。

国防部无需从零开始构建这一学习架构。部队内部的一些领域已经存在经过验证的模式。例如，海军陆战队作战实验室与作战人员密切合作，对新系统进行测试和分析。使用者的视角在技术开发流程的早期就被融入其中，从而使系统能够快速列装。即便针对同样的作战能力缺口，这种开发方式也能比正式立项的采办项目进展更快。

但以作战人员为中心的做法不应仅限于正式的军事创新机构。由使用者提供信息的分析必须扩展到整个国防生态体系，从而加快集成、缩短采办周期并推广可信的成果。

这并非仅凭断言。当采办奏效时——无论是快速采办还是其他形式——部分原因就在于分析人员曾进入战壕、登上飞机，或置身作战信息中心，从作战人员的视角评估、验证采办工作并为其提供依据。

我之所以知道，是因为我的分析人员曾主导过这类卓有成效的工作。我们在真实环境中设计并实施了原型测试，对性能进行独立技术分析。战术前沿的分析工作发现了作战人员安全使用系统之前必须解决的关键问题，也揭示了制造商未曾预料到的系统新战术用途。

“伊拉克自由行动”和“持久自由行动”中反简易爆炸装置作战的复杂性提供了一个明确的例证：仅凭作战人员的反馈不足以评估某项技术的效用。当时有太多反简易爆炸装置系统被推给作战人员，因此弄清哪些系统在哪些条件下有效变得至关重要。

然而，分析中最具挑战性的问题之一是对“未发生之事”加以证明。换言之，如果一枚简易爆炸装置没有爆炸，那是因为反简易爆炸装置系统起了作用，还是并非如此？我们的分析人员与海军陆战队部队一同部署以收集数据，并运用复杂的统计方法作出判断。当时人命攸关，我们的分析发挥了作用。

国防部转向作战采办系统既必要又及时。未来战场上的胜利属于能够通过快速采办和战时适应创造军事优势的国家。这一点很清楚。但持久的快速并非仅靠流程重新设计就能实现，而是来自构建一个向作战人员学习的采办体系——在那里，数据是模拟式的，结果需要深刻洞察才能解读。

如果国防部充分整合这样一个学习闭环，其成效将不止于缩短周期。它将打造出一支适应更快、集成更好、能够按战争所需的速度交付与作战相关能力的部队。采办改革正是由此转化为作战优势。

凯瑟琳·A·麦格雷迪（Katherine A. McGrady）博士是 CNA 的总裁兼首席执行官，CNA 运营着海军分析中心（Center for Naval Analyses），这是一个联邦资助研发中心，曾在第二次世界大战期间为支持美国海军而开创了作战分析领域。

items.title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft arrive at Creech AFB, advancing operational integration
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: The aircraft will undergo Air Combat Command-led operational experimentation to evaluate uncrewed systems and refine operational employment alongside crewed combat aircraft.
items.body:
Published Sept. 24, 2026

Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs

The Air Force received its first two Collaborative Combat Aircraft at Creech Air Force Base , Nevada, marking a significant step toward integrating uncrewed, semi-autonomous aircraft into future combat operations. Anduril delivered the first CCA, the YFQ-44A, to the Experimental Operations Unit last month, and General Atomics delivered the YFQ-42A last week. The aircraft will support Air Combat Command -led operational experimentation to refine how CCA will be employed alongside crewed aircraft in contested environments.

items.titleZh: 协同作战飞机抵达Creech AFB，推进作战一体化
items.summaryZh: 该型飞机将接受空军作战司令部主导的作战试验，以评估无人系统，并完善其与有人作战飞机协同运用的方式。
items.zhFull:
发布于2026年9月24日

空军部长公共事务办公室

美国空军在位于内华达州的克里奇空军基地接收了首批两架协同作战飞机（CCA），这标志着在将无人、半自主飞机纳入未来作战行动方面迈出了重要一步。安杜里尔公司上个月向实验作战部队交付了首架 CCA——YFQ-44A，通用原子公司上周交付了 YFQ-42A。这些飞机将支持由空战司令部主导的作战实验，以完善 CCA 如何在对抗环境中与有人驾驶飞机协同运用。

items.title: With Denmark, Saildrone logs first flag registration for naval surveillance drone
items.author: Jaroslaw Adamowski
items.summary: U.S. naval drone maker Saildrone seeks to expand its footprint in Europe, with Denmark a key customer in the contested Baltic and North seas.
items.body:
WARSAW, Poland — U.S. company Saildrone has announced that the first four Voyager unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) have been registered under the Danish flag, marking the first time the producer’s vehicle operate under a national flag.

The development comes as Saildrone is working with partners in the Netherlands, Norway and Poland to ramp up its USV production for European customers, including militaries.

Kim Løye Sørensen, the European head of business development at Saildrone Denmark, the company’s subsidiary that manages its operations in Europe, told Defense News the firm is observing a rising demand for surface drones across the continent, and is in talks with a number of navies.

“We’ve had a collaboration with the Danish Navy where we had four of our Voyager platforms … in operation for the Danish Navy for a six-month period,” Sørensen said. “Now the Danish Navy and the Danish government are in the process of creating a new contract to have more Saildrones within the Danish Armed Forces. But in the near future we also see our drones operating in different European countries in the northern part of Europe.”

Due to Denmark’s location between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea, the Royal Danish Navy plays a strategic role in monitoring and safeguarding maritime traffic through the Danish Straits, a gateway between the two seas.

The 33-foot Voyager is designed for coastal surveillance and nearshore mapping missions, performing continuous maritime intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), seafloor characterization, as well as real-time domain awareness, according to data from Saildrone. Powered by an electric motor and enabled with a mapping speed of 5 knots, the USV can operate for 100 days between service stops.

Voyager USVs can perform “maritime domain awareness and the ISR for a long period of time. More than three months out in station and being out there without doing anything, just being a forwarding sensor providing the data,” Sørensen said.

In addition to the Voyager, Explorer and Surveyor platforms, Saildrone is also developing a new product, Spectre, a 170-foot USV that will join the portfolio as its largest and fastest platform that will carry weapons.

“With our Spectre platform, there will be kinetic effectors,” Sørensen said. “It’s a container-based solution. You could either have two 40-foot containers or five 20-foot containers of various payloads, including kinetics on that platform. That will be built in 2027.”

Jaroslaw Adamowski is the Poland correspondent for Defense News.
items.titleZh: 与丹麦合作，Saildrone完成海军监视无人机的首次船旗注册
items.summaryZh: 美国海军无人机厂商Saildrone寻求扩大在欧洲的业务布局，丹麦是其在争夺激烈的波罗的海和北海地区的关键客户。
items.zhFull:
波兰华沙——美国公司Saildrone宣布，首批四艘Voyager无人水面艇（USV）已在丹麦登记并悬挂丹麦国旗，这标志着该生产商的艇首次在一国国旗下运行。

这一进展正值Saildrone与荷兰、挪威和波兰的合作伙伴共同努力，以提高面向欧洲客户（包括军方）的USV产量。

Saildrone Denmark——该公司负责欧洲业务的子公司——的欧洲业务开发主管金·洛伊·索伦森（Kim Løye Sørensen）告诉《国防新闻》，该公司正观察到整个欧洲对水面无人艇的需求不断上升，并正与多国海军进行商谈。

“我们曾与丹麦海军合作，在此期间我们有四套Voyager平台……为丹麦海军运行了六个月，”索伦森说。“现在丹麦海军和丹麦政府正在制定一份新合同，以便让丹麦武装部队拥有更多Saildrone。但在不久的将来，我们还将看到我们的无人艇在欧洲北部的多个欧洲国家运行。”

由于丹麦地处波罗的海和北海之间，丹麦皇家海军在监测和保障经由丹麦海峡的海上交通方面发挥着战略作用，该海峡是两海之间的门户。

根据Saildrone的数据，33-foot的Voyager旨在执行沿海监视和近岸测绘任务，持续进行海上情报、监视与侦察（ISR）、海床表征以及实时态势感知。该USV由电动机驱动，测绘速度为5 knots，在两次维护停靠之间可运行100 days。

索伦森说，Voyager USV能够长期执行“海上态势感知和ISR。在站位部署超过三个月，在那里待着无需做任何事情，只是作为一个转发传感器提供数据”。

除Voyager、Explorer和Surveyor平台外，Saildrone还在开发一款新产品Spectre，这是一艘170-foot的USV，将作为其最大、最快的平台加入产品组合，并将携带武器。

“在我们的 Spectre 平台上，将会有动能效应器，”索伦森（Sørensen）说。“这是一种基于集装箱的解决方案。你可以选择两个 40-foot 集装箱，或者五个 20-foot 集装箱，搭载各种有效载荷，包括该平台上的动能效应器。它将在 2027 年建造。”

雅罗斯瓦夫·阿达莫夫斯基（Jaroslaw Adamowski）是《防务新闻》驻波兰记者。

items.title: Report: CIA warned Europe of Russian drone attack from vessels in the Mediterranean
items.author: Linus Höller
items.summary: The CIA reportedly warned European nations of a suspected Russian plot to launch explosive drones from aboard commercial vessels in the Mediterranean.
items.body:
VIENNA — The CIA has warned European countries of a suspected Russian plot to launch Gerbera-type drones from aboard commercial vessels in the Mediterranean, a new report says.

Major Spanish daily El Mundo published the article, which was based on testimony from an anonymous Lithuanian intelligence source, late Wednesday local time.

According to the paper, the CIA had assessed that Spain, France or Italy may be the targets of these attacks, with drones launching from international waters in the Mediterranean and traveling to the coastal countries over the course of an hour or two.

The Gerbera drone was selected because of its small size – it has a wingspan of just 2.5 meters – which allows it to be concealed easily, El Mundo wrote. The drones have a maximum range of 600 kilometers, depending on load and environmental conditions, and carry a relatively small warhead that would be effective at starting a fire, destroying exposed infrastructure components or causing political and economic turmoil.

The drones were to be transported hidden in containers, which was described as being “not difficult at all,” before being catapult-launched for their attack missions on the Western Mediterranean NATO members, according to El Mundo’s sourcing.

Lithuania and other European countries were reportedly made aware of this threat shortly after the CIA director made an unannounced and secretive visit to Moscow aboard a U.S. military plane on Aug. 25.

According to El Mundo, an key CIA report was rumored to be circulating in European leadership circles in mid-September, coinciding with French President Emmanuel Macron’s decision to convene the Defense Council on Sept. 16 and then summon all party leaders and the 2027 presidential candidates to the Élysée Palace two days later.

The El Mundo report has not been independently corroborated.

The perceived threat of Russian kinetic action has increased significantly across European capitals this year, owing to heightened sabotage and hybrid warfare activity generally attributed to Moscow. Airspace violations by Russian drones along NATO’s eastern flank have become increasingly commonplace, leading to several instances of the alliance’s fighter jets shooting down intruding unmanned aerial vehicles.

A year ago, 19 unarmed Russian drones entered Polish airspace, the largest airspace violation to date, and one that was widely assessed to have been a deliberate provocation and test of NATO’s response.

The prospect of launching from Russian merchant ships has long been suspected in European policy circles, with coastal sightings of unidentified UAVs sometimes coinciding with the presence of Russian “shadow fleet” ships. In February of this year, a Swedish Navy vessel detected and jammed a drone taking off from a Russian intelligence ship in the Öresund Strait, coinciding with a visit of the French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle to the Scandinavian country.

A new step on the escalation ladder was reached in early August, when an explosive-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo aircraft and a separate plane collided with a drone mid-air at Germany’s Leipzig airport, a key freight hub in the NATO country. After a month-long investigation, German authorities officially attributed the attack to Russia.

On Sept. 19, the major pro-Russian Telegram channel Rybar published a map titled “Russian medicine against French arrogance,” suggesting supplying Algeria with Geran-5 drones to strike French aeronautical factories, military bases, nuclear plants and petrochemical sites, El Mundo reported.

Even non-NATO, landlocked European countries are taking note and stepping up their preparedness. The Austrian military has launched a “large exercise” to practice counter-drone measures and air defense, Austrian public media reported on Thursday. The drill will involve 300 soldiers spread across several townships in eastern Austria, as well as Mistral ground-to-air missiles, 35-millimeter cannons and electronic warfare measures.

Linus Höller is Defense News' Europe correspondent and OSINT investigator. He reports on the arms deals, sanctions, and geopolitics shaping Europe and the world. He holds master’s degrees in WMD nonproliferation, terrorism studies, and international relations, and works in four languages: English, German, Russian, and Spanish.
items.titleZh: 报道：中情局曾就俄罗斯从地中海船只发动无人机袭击警告欧洲
items.summaryZh: 据报道，中情局曾警告欧洲国家，怀疑俄罗斯策划从地中海商船上发射爆炸性无人机。
items.zhFull:
维也纳——一份新报告称，CIA已警告欧洲国家，怀疑俄罗斯策划从地中海商船上发射Gerbera型无人机。

西班牙主要日报《世界报》（El Mundo）于当地时间周三晚些时候发表了这篇文章，文章基于一名匿名的立陶宛情报消息源的证词。

据该报称，CIA评估认为，西班牙、法国或意大利可能是这些袭击的目标，无人机将从地中海国际水域发射，并在一到两个小时内飞抵这些沿海国家。

《世界报》写道，选择Gerbera无人机是因为其体积小——翼展仅2.5米——这使其易于隐藏。该型无人机最大航程为600公里，取决于载荷和环境条件，并携带相对较小的弹头，这种弹头足以引发火灾、摧毁暴露的基础设施部件或造成政治和经济动荡。

据《世界报》的消息源称，这些无人机将被隐藏在集装箱中运输，据称这“一点也不困难”，随后将通过弹射方式发射，执行对西地中海北约成员国的袭击任务。

据报道，在CIA局长于8月25日乘坐一架美军飞机对莫斯科进行未经宣布的秘密访问后不久，立陶宛和其他欧洲国家便获悉了这一威胁。

据《世界报》称，有传言称，一份重要的CIA报告于9月中旬在欧洲领导层圈子里流传，恰逢法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙（Emmanuel Macron）决定在9月16日召开国防委员会会议，并在两天后召集所有政党领导人和2027年总统候选人前往爱丽舍宫。

《世界报》的报道尚未得到独立证实。

今年，由于通常被归咎于莫斯科的破坏和混合战争活动加剧，欧洲各国首都对俄罗斯动能行动的威胁感知显著上升。俄罗斯无人机沿北约东翼侵犯领空的行为日益普遍，导致该联盟的战斗机多次击落入侵的无人机。

一年前，19架未携带武器的俄罗斯无人机进入波兰领空，这是迄今为止规模最大的一次领空侵犯，并被广泛评估为一次蓄意挑衅和对北约反应的测试。

长期以来，欧洲政策圈一直怀疑存在从俄罗斯商船发射无人机的可能性，沿海目击不明无人机的事件有时与俄罗斯“影子舰队”船只的出现同时发生。今年2月，一艘瑞典海军舰艇在厄勒海峡探测并干扰了一架从俄罗斯情报船起飞的无人机，当时正值法国航母“夏尔·戴高乐”号（Charles de Gaulle）访问这个斯堪的纳维亚国家。

8月初，局势升级阶梯上又迈出了一步：一架满载爆炸物的无人机在乌克兰货机附近被发现，另一架飞机在德国莱比锡机场与一架无人机空中相撞；莱比锡机场是这个北约国家的重要货运枢纽。经过长达一个月的调查，德国当局正式将这起袭击归咎于俄罗斯。

据El Mundo报道，9月19日，亲俄罗斯的主要Telegram频道Rybar发布了一张标题为“俄罗斯对付法国傲慢的良药”的地图，建议向阿尔及利亚提供Geran-5无人机，以打击法国航空工厂、军事基地、核电站和石化设施。

就连非北约的内陆欧洲国家也在关注并加强防备。奥地利公共媒体周四报道，奥地利军方已启动一场“大规模演习”，以演练反无人机措施和防空。此次演习将涉及分布在奥地利东部多个乡镇的300名士兵，以及Mistral地空导弹、35-millimeter火炮和电子战措施。

利努斯·赫勒（Linus Höller）是《Defense News》的欧洲通讯员和开源情报（OSINT）调查员。他报道塑造欧洲和世界的军火交易、制裁和地缘政治。他拥有大规模杀伤性武器防扩散、恐怖主义研究和国际关系专业的硕士学位，并以四种语言工作：英语、德语、俄语和西班牙语。

items.title: Risk Factors Measured Around Age 60 as Predictors of Dementia Around Age 80 in the U.S.
items.author: Susann Rohwedder
items.summary: We estimated the probability of dementia at age 80 as a function of risk factors measured at age 60, using a recently developed and validated probabilistic dementia measure and longitudinal regression models.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 24, 2026Published in: AJE Advances: Research in Epidemiology, uuag036 (2026). DOI: 10.1093/ajeadv/uuag036

The number of older adults living with dementia in the United States and worldwide continues to rise. Identifying elevated dementia risk decades before potential onset can help individuals prepare and enable healthcare providers and policymakers to target resources that may delay onset or mitigate consequences. Using nationally representative data from the U.S. Health and Retirement Study (1992-2016), we estimated the probability of dementia at around age 80 as a function of 110 risk factors measured at around age 60, using a recently developed and validated probabilistic dementia measure and longitudinal regression models. Poor physical health, low cognitive ability, fewer than 12 years of education, and greater functional limitations at around age 60 were the strongest predictors of dementia at age 80. Additional predictors included being born in the Southeastern U.S., lacking private health insurance, non-veteran status, having poor vision or hearing, limited work history, disability, diabetes, body mass index ≥ 35, prior stroke, and both alcohol abstention and heavy drinking. Several predictors, such as geographic origin, veteran status, and work history, have received limited attention in prior prediction research. Future research should examine whether these candidate predictors represent causal risk factors rather than simply associations.

- Document Number: EP-71487

items.titleZh: 美国60岁前后测得的风险因素对80岁前后痴呆症的预测作用
items.summaryZh: 我们使用近期开发并经验证的痴呆概率测量方法和纵向回归模型，将80岁时的痴呆概率估计为60岁时所测风险因素的函数。

在美国和全球，患有痴呆症的老年人数量持续上升。在可能发病前数十年识别出痴呆风险升高，可以帮助个人做好准备，并使医疗服务提供者和政策制定者能够将资源投向可能延缓发病或减轻后果的领域。我们使用美国健康与退休研究（1992-2016）中具有全国代表性的数据，采用近期开发并验证的概率性痴呆测量指标和纵向回归模型，估算了80岁左右患痴呆症的概率；该概率是60岁左右测量的110项风险因素的函数。60岁左右身体健康状况差、认知能力低、受教育年限少于12年以及功能受限较多，是80岁时患痴呆症的最强预测因素。其他预测因素包括：出生于美国东南部、缺乏私人医疗保险、非退伍军人身份、视力或听力差、工作经历有限、残疾、糖尿病、体重指数 ≥ 35、既往中风，以及戒酒和大量饮酒。若干预测因素，如地理来源、退伍军人身份和工作经历，在既往预测研究中受到的关注有限。未来研究应考察这些候选预测因素是否代表因果风险因素，而不仅仅是关联。

items.title: Estimating the Cost of Early Colleges
items.author: Brian Phillips
items.summary: In this paper, we assess the costs of the early college model in North Carolina relative to costs for typical high school education.
items.body:
Three Complementary Approaches

ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 24, 2026Published in: American Journal of Evaluation (2026). DOI: 10.1177/10982140261479706

Early college high schools offer students many dual enrollment courses and the opportunity to earn an associate degree while in high school. In this paper, we assess the costs of the early college model in North Carolina relative to costs for typical high school education. We use three complementary approaches: one using administrative expenditure data from high schools and colleges across the state, one using the ingredients method based on in-depth subject matter expert interviews in five case study districts, and a third “hybrid” approach combining the two methods. Our findings suggest that educating an early college student incurs higher relative costs in high school that are offset by lower costs to a college degree for students who eventually complete a postsecondary credential. However, excess credit attainment attenuates the postsecondary savings. We discuss the implications of these findings for implementation of the early college model and for cost study methodologies.

items.titleZh: 估算早期大学的成本
items.summaryZh: 在本文中，我们评估了北卡罗来纳州早期大学模式的成本，并与典型高中教育的成本进行了比较。
items.zhFull:
三种互补方法

研究发布于 rand.org，2026年9月24日；刊载于：《美国评估杂志》（2026年）。DOI: 10.1177/10982140261479706

早期大学高中为学生提供大量双学分课程，以及在高中的同时获得副学士学位的机会。本文评估北卡罗来纳州早期大学模式的成本，并与普通高中教育的成本相比较。我们采用三种互补方法：一种是使用全州高中和高校的行政支出数据，一种是基于五个案例研究学区深入专家访谈的要素法，第三种是结合上述两种方法的“混合”方法。我们的研究结果显示，培养一名早期大学学生在高中阶段会产生相对较高的成本，但对最终获得高等教育学历的学生而言，这些成本会被取得大学学位的较低成本所抵消。然而，超额获得的学分削弱了高等教育阶段的节省。我们讨论了这些发现对早期大学模式实施以及成本研究方法的启示。

items.title: Disconnection Among American Youth
items.author: Stephanie Bonds
items.summary: Periods of disconnection (not engaged in education, training, or work) are costly for young people and for society. This paper presents findings from a survey of 349 young adults aged 18 to 22 to inform programs designed for this at-risk population.
items.body:
Evidence on Its Duration and Impact on Well-Being

Expert InsightsPublished Sep 24, 2026

Periods of disconnection (not engaged in education, training, or work) are costly for young people and for society. Designing programs to serve the one in every three young adults aged 18 to 22 who experiences disconnection requires a better understanding of when and how disconnection occurs. This paper presents survey results of 349 young adults to inform such programs and show how disconnection relates to social interaction and mental health.

One in three young Americans experiences disconnection after high school—and for many, it lasts at least six months.

After high school, many young people hit stretches of time when they’re not engaged in school, training, or work. These periods—called disconnection—are costly for young people and for society. But relatively little is known about how long disconnection typically lasts or how it shapes young people’s broader well-being.

RAND researchers used survey data from the American Youth Panel to trace patterns of disconnection among 18- to 22-year-olds, identify who is most likely to experience the longest spells, and examine how disconnection relates to social interaction and mental health.

Nearly one in four young adults reported disconnection lasting at least six months; about 11 percent reported spells of a year or more.

Nearly one in four disconnected young men reported that their mental health was “not good” every day of the prior month.

About two-thirds of young men experiencing disconnection reported no in-person time with friends in the prior week—a stark contrast to their peers who had never been disconnected.

For disconnected young men especially, the findings suggest that education and employment programs alone may miss critical needs around social isolation and well-being.

items.title: Army awards Palantir $48.1M to modernize ammo management
items.author: Daniel Terrill
items.summary: The tech company has built AI software designed to process data for targeting and decision-making, and now, managing ammo.
items.body:
The U.S. Army awarded a subsidiary of Palantir Technologies a $48.1 million contract to develop software designed to improve how the service tracks and manages ammunition.

According to last week’s announcement, the new software will streamline ammunition management by consolidating nine separate legacy platforms.

“Ultimately, this system is one element to modernize overall ammunition systems, retire legacy systems and improve audit readiness,” the service said.

The software will use “commercial low-code, no-code technology” and give soldiers the ability to track munitions throughout their lifecycle, the Army said.

That includes everything from “planning, production, and procurement, to storage, surveillance, distribution, expenditure, and final disposition,” according to the service.

The contract comes as the Army works to address longstanding problems with its ammunition management systems.

In March, the Army’s Line of Departure journal published an article describing shortcomings in the service’s existing ammunition processes, including inaccurate forecasting and disconnected digital systems.

According to the article, ammunition forecasts at lower levels often rely on assumptions and historical trends rather than actual demand tied to training cycles.

The legacy systems also operate independently, meaning changes to training schedules may not be reflected across the ammunition management process in real time.

“The result is an accountability model failing to meet the operational tempo or digital expectations of the modern force,” the article says.

Over the past few years alone, Palantir has led or contributed to several programs for integrating artificial intelligence into workflows and decision-making, including Army Vantage, Next Generation Command and Control and the Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node.

However, Palantir might be best known for the Maven Smart System, or MSS, an AI-enabled system used by all branches of service that’s designed to present intelligence data to enhance operational decisions like targeting options.

For the ammo management software, the Army said Palantir beat out the competition through a three-phase selection process over a six-week period.

“Vendors were evaluated on key capabilities including integrating data from disparate legacy systems, the ability to provide robust planning and forecast models, and support tactical users in disconnected or low-bandwidth environments,” the Army said.

Under the agreement, Palantir will develop the new software over the next 12 months and provide support for an additional five years.

Daniel Terrill is a contributor to Military Times. He’s been reporting on military issues, the gun industry, and the outdoors for nearly two decades. Although writing is his passion, he’s been a Marine, police officer, and, perhaps the most dangerous job of his career, a substitute teacher.
items.titleZh: 陆军授予Palantir 4810万美元合同，用于弹药管理现代化
items.summaryZh: 这家科技公司已开发出人工智能软件，用于处理目标定位与决策所需数据，如今又用于弹药管理。
items.zhFull:
美国陆军向 Palantir Technologies 的一家子公司授予一份价值 4810 万美元的合同，用于开发旨在改进陆军追踪和管理弹药方式的软件。

根据上周发布的公告，这款新软件将整合九个各自独立的遗留平台，从而简化弹药管理。

陆军表示：“最终，该系统是实现整体弹药系统现代化、淘汰遗留系统并提高审计准备状态的一个环节。”

陆军表示，该软件将采用“商用低代码、无代码技术”，使士兵能够追踪弹药的全寿命周期。

据陆军称，这涵盖从“规划、生产和采购，到储存、监控、分发、消耗和最终处置”的各个环节。

这份合同的签订，正值陆军着力解决其弹药管理系统长期存在的问题之际。

今年 3 月，陆军的《Line of Departure》杂志刊登了一篇文章，描述了陆军现有弹药流程的种种不足，包括预测不准确和数字系统彼此脱节。

据该文章称，较低层级的弹药预测往往依赖假设和历史趋势，而非与训练周期挂钩的实际需求。

这些遗留系统还独立运行，这意味着训练计划的变化可能无法实时反映到整个弹药管理流程中。

“其结果是，这种问责模式无法满足现代部队的作战节奏或数字期望，”文章称。

仅在过去几年里，Palantir就领导或参与了好几个将人工智能融入工作流程和决策的项目，包括陆军Vantage、下一代指挥与控制以及战术情报目标接入节点。

然而，Palantir最为人所知的可能是Maven Smart System（MSS），这是一个所有军种都在使用的人工智能赋能系统，旨在呈现情报数据，以增强诸如目标选择方案等作战决策。

对于弹药管理软件，陆军表示，Palantir在为期六周、分三阶段的遴选过程中击败了竞争对手。

“供应商是按关键能力接受评估的，包括整合来自不同遗留系统的数据、提供稳健的规划和预测模型，以及在断连或低带宽环境中支持战术用户，”陆军表示。

根据协议，Palantir将在未来12个月内开发这款新软件，并在此后额外提供五年支持。

丹尼尔·特里尔（Daniel Terrill）是《军事时报》的撰稿人。他报道军事问题、枪支行业和户外领域已近二十年。尽管写作是他的热情所在，但他还曾是一名海军陆战队队员、一名警察，以及——或许是他职业生涯中最危险的工作——一名代课教师。

“其结果是，这种问责模式无法满足现代部队的作战节奏或数字期望，”文章称。
仅在过去几年里，Palantir就领导或参与了好几个将人工智能融入工作流程和决策的项目，包括陆军Vantage、下一代指挥与控制以及战术情报目标接入节点。
然而，Palantir最为人所知的可能是Maven Smart System（MSS），这是一个所有军种都在使用的人工智能赋能系统，旨在呈现情报数据，以增强诸如目标选择方案等作战决策。
对于弹药管理软件，陆军表示，Palantir在为期六周、分三阶段的遴选过程中击败了竞争对手。
“供应商是按关键能力接受评估的，包括整合来自不同遗留系统的数据、提供稳健的规划和预测模型，以及在断连或低带宽环境中支持战术用户，”陆军表示。
根据协议，Palantir将在未来12个月内开发这款新软件，并在此后额外提供五年支持。
丹尼尔·特里尔（Daniel Terrill）是《军事时报》的撰稿人。他报道军事问题、枪支行业和户外领域已近二十年。尽管写作是他的热情所在，但他还曾是一名海军陆战队队员、一名警察，以及——或许是他职业生涯中最危险的工作——一名代课教师。

items.title: Steam catapults? US Navy appears to be sticking with electromagnetics on carriers
items.author: Michael Peck
items.summary: Despite an August order for the U.S. Navy to return to steam catapults on its newest carriers, the service appears to be sticking with electromagnetics.
items.body:
Despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s nostalgia for old-fashioned steam catapults, the U.S. Navy appears to be sticking with electromagnetics for its newest class of aircraft carriers.

The Navy recently awarded contracts for the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System, or EMALS, which uses electrically generated magnetic fields to launch aircraft from Ford-class carriers.

Kato Engineering was awarded a $49.3 million contract this week to support the energy storage subsystem of EMALS. The Navy also published a sources sought notice on Wednesday, seeking vendors to supply components such as EMALS recirculation pumps.

The Navy maintains that electromagnetic catapults provide smoother acceleration, can be adjusted to launch various types of aircraft such as drones, can be reset for faster launches and require less maintenance and personnel. China, meanwhile, is equipping its new Fujian-class carriers with electromagnetic catapults.

Trump resurrected the steam catapult versus EMALS conversation in August, when he ordered the Navy to replace EMALS with the older system on the USS Doris Miller, the next Ford-class carrier under construction.

In an August memo, Trump pointed at a Navy that has suffered from “a series of shipbuilding setbacks stemming from overly complex designs and iterative design change procedures, which have resulted in cost growth, delays, and cancellations.”

The president suggested mandating that the Navy submit “a plan on the required measures to replace the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System and Advanced Weapons Elevators with steam and hydraulic systems for the construction of CVN-81 [USS Doris Miller], including timelines and resourcing requirements.”

The White House’s order baffled naval experts. The Navy has not ordered a steam catapult in 20 years, with the last order placed for the USS George H. W. Bush, commissioned in 2009 as the final Nimitz-class carrier.

Finding a manufacturer for steam catapults, and then redesigning Ford-class carriers to accept them, would likely require sweeping manufacturing overhauls at considerable expense, critics of the order said.

Despite their planned phasing out, steam catapults are a proven technology. They were developed by Britain in the 1950s to replace the hydraulic catapults of World War II-era carriers and were later copied by the U.S.

“The decision was made in April 1952 that the steam catapult would probably be the most satisfactory type for a service catapult,” noted a 1954 article in the U.S. Naval Institute magazine Proceedings. “Arrangements were made for the manufacturing rights to the British catapult. British drawings were obtained and redrawn to U. S. standards and modified to fit U.S. naval requirements.”

Manufactured for 21st century carriers, EMALS “is designed to expand the operational capability of Ford-class carriers, providing the Navy with capability for launching all current and future carrier air wing platforms – lightweight unmanned to heavy strike fighters.

The rapid evolution of unmanned aircraft, which may soon become the backbone of carrier air wings, will likely require a more sophisticated launch system. Recent contracts suggest the U.S. Navy is planning accordingly.

Michael Peck is a correspondent for Defense News and a columnist for the Center for European Policy Analysis. He holds an M.A. in political science from Rutgers University. Find him at theuncommondefense.com. His email is mikedefense1@gmail.com.
items.titleZh: 蒸汽弹射器？美国海军似乎在航母上坚持使用电磁弹射
items.summaryZh: 尽管8月有一项要求美国海军在其最新航母上重新使用蒸汽弹射器的命令，但该军种似乎仍坚持使用电磁弹射。
items.zhFull:
尽管美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）怀念老式蒸汽弹射器，但美国海军似乎仍将为其最新一级航空母舰坚持采用电磁弹射系统。

美国海军最近授予了电磁飞机弹射系统（Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System，EMALS）相关合同，该系统利用电磁产生的磁场从福特级航母上弹射飞机。

Kato Engineering 本周获得一份价值 4930 万美元的合同，为 EMALS 的储能子系统提供支持。美国海军周三还发布了一份来源征集通知，寻求供应商提供 EMALS 再循环泵等部件。

美国海军坚持认为，电磁弹射器提供更平稳的加速，可调整以弹射无人机等各类飞机，可更快重置以加快弹射，且所需维护和人员更少。与此同时，中国正在为其新型福建级航母配备电磁弹射器。

特朗普在8月重新挑起蒸汽弹射器与 EMALS 之争，当时他下令美国海军在建的下一艘福特级航母 USS Doris Miller 上以较老的系统取代 EMALS。

在8月的一份备忘录中，特朗普指出，美国海军遭遇了“一系列造船挫折，其根源在于过度复杂的设计和反复的设计变更程序，这些已导致成本增长、延误和取消。”

总统建议强制要求美国海军提交“一份关于为建造 CVN-81 [USS Doris Miller] 用以蒸汽和液压系统取代电磁飞机弹射系统和先进武器升降机所需措施的计划，包括时间表和资源需求。”

白宫的命令令海军专家困惑。美国海军已有20年未订购蒸汽弹射器，上一次订购是为 USS George H. W. Bush 号，该舰于2009年服役，是最后一艘 Nimitz 级航母。

反对这一命令的批评者表示，为蒸汽弹射器找到制造商，然后重新设计福特级航母以适配蒸汽弹射器，很可能需要大范围的制造业改造，且代价高昂。

尽管蒸汽弹射器计划被逐步淘汰，但它是一项经过验证的技术。它由英国于20世纪50年代研发，用于取代二战时期航母上的液压弹射器，后来被美国仿制。

“1952年4月作出的决定认为，蒸汽弹射器很可能最适合作为部队使用的弹射器，”美国海军学会杂志《Proceedings》1954年的一篇文章指出。“随后就英国弹射器的制造权作出了安排。美方获取了英国的图纸，按美国标准重新绘制，并加以修改以满足美国海军的需求。”

作为为21世纪航母制造的装备，EMALS“旨在拓展福特级航母的作战能力，使海军具备弹射当前及未来所有航母航空联队平台的能力——从轻型无人机到重型打击战斗机。

无人机的快速演进可能很快使其成为航母航空联队的骨干，这很可能需要一套更先进的弹射系统。近期签订的合同表明，美国海军正据此作出规划。

迈克尔·佩克（Michael Peck）是《防务新闻》的通讯员，也是欧洲政策分析中心的专栏作家。他拥有罗格斯大学政治学硕士学位。可在 theuncommondefense.com 找到他。他的电子邮箱是 mikedefense1@gmail.com。

items.title: Air Force, civilian staff dispute status of China Aerospace Studies Institute
items.author: Michael Scanlon
items.summary: CASI's director said the move will effectively end the institute, even as the service says CASI’s mission will continue.
items.body:
On Oct. 1, the Air Force will eliminate all 10 civilian positions at the China Aerospace Studies Institute, the Air University center that publishes unclassified research on the People’s Liberation Army’s air, space and missile forces. Its director said the move will effectively end the institute, even as the service says CASI’s mission will continue.

“As a part of the ongoing civilian restructure within Air Education and Training Command, civilian positions will no longer be assigned to China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI),” an Air Force spokesperson said in a statement to Defense News on Tuesday. “The CASI mission continues, with the organization leveraging assigned military service members to accomplish its objectives.”

Civilians affected by the restructuring will stay in their current positions until further notice and will be evaluated for reassignment, the spokesperson said.

CASI Director Brendan Mulvaney described the fallout differently. All of the institute’s civilian billets are being eliminated, “effectively ending CASI,” he said Tuesday. No military positions are affected, he said, noting the institute has two master sergeant billets and a deputy position that has remained unfilled for over a year.

Asked how the cut would impact the institute’s research, Mulvaney said, “All of the research has always been done by the civilian personnel.”

According to Mulvaney, the decision was made by the previous Air University commander and forwarded by AETC under a requirement to cut civilian jobs across the Department of the Air Force. The quota originated with the Air Force’s manpower and reserve affairs office, he said.

The cut “had nothing to do with CASI’s mission,” Mulvaney said, but due to the fact that the institute does not produce professional military education students, which is Air University’s primary mission.

Asked whether another organization would take on CASI’s China aerospace research, Mulvaney said, “Nothing has been identified.” It is also unknown whether CASI’s reports, translations and course materials will remain publicly available, or whether its website will remain online, he said.

The cuts became public Monday, when a note from a CASI civilian circulated on social media. The employee wrote that every CASI civilian position would be unfunded as of Oct. 1 and that the staff would become “surplus federal employees,” a federal personnel term for workers whose positions are being eliminated.

The note described CASI’s future as “uncertain,” adding that “CASI punched above its weight given our small team and budget.”

Will Yale, a Navy surface warfare officer who posted the note on X, wrote that it was “extremely unfortunate and regrettable” that the Department of the Air Force “has decided to shutter” CASI. He described the institute as one of the most prominent in its field and wrote that it had “measurably increased knowledge about the PLA” inside the U.S. government and outside it.

Andrew Erickson, a Naval War College professor and CASI associate, noted that the news is “specific to CASI only.” Mulvaney said the action does not affect the Navy’s China Maritime Studies Institute, the Army War College’s China Landpower Studies Center or the Marine Corps War College’s China Warfighting Initiative.

CASI was established in 2017 and formally chartered on June 15, 2021, by then-Chief of Staff Gen. Charles Q. Brown Jr. The charter tasked the institute with studying “everything that flies” in China, calling CASI the Air Force’s leading center for the study of China and its aerospace capabilities. It has offices at Maxwell Air Force Base, Alabama, and Fort McNair in Washington.

The institute’s research was unclassified by design, according to its charter, which directed CASI to use publicly available native-language sources and publish its findings. CASI translated PLA textbooks and doctrine, published reference primers and ran a free three-day PLA Fundamentals course that required no security clearance.

Its biennial CASI Conference, held in May at National Defense University, drew more than 250 attendees and featured the release of the fifth edition of its “PLA Aerospace Power” primer, CASI said.

In 2025, nearly 80,000 people visited CASI’s website and downloaded more than 50,000 reports, according to the institute. The site remains live and posted a new paper on Sept. 21, “From Vision to Vigilance: How Beijing’s Space-Science Roadmap Builds a Real-Time Kill Web.”

CASI had already lost staff a year ago. In an October 2025 quarterly update, the institute said a Defense Department efficiency drive had eliminated its director of education and education program manager positions as the Department of the Air Force was “reorganizing, inactivating, and realigning organizations.” CASI said things were “in flux” and it would provide a status update once it knew more.

Ryan Fedasiuk, a fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, called the move “a devastating loss for the analytic community” and an “incomprehensible decision.”

The Air Force said CASI’s mission will continue, with military members carrying on the work Mulvaney said civilians have always done.

Michael Scanlon is a defense journalist covering air and space warfare. A former U.S. Air Force A-10 crew chief, he has supported land and sea programs for the U.S. Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard.
items.titleZh: 空军与文职人员就中国航空航天研究所的地位产生争议
items.summaryZh: CASI主任表示，此举将实际终结该研究所，即便空军称CASI的使命仍将继续。
items.zhFull:
10月1日，美国空军将裁撤中国航空航天研究所（China Aerospace Studies Institute）的全部10个文职岗位。该研究所是空军大学下设中心，负责发布有关中国人民解放军空中、太空和导弹力量的机密研究。该研究所所长表示，此举将实际上终止该研究所，尽管空军方面称CASI的任务仍将继续。

“作为空军教育与训练司令部正在进行的文职人员重组的一部分，将不再向中国航空航天研究所（CASI）分配文职岗位，”一名空军发言人周二在给《防务新闻》的声明中说。“CASI的任务仍在继续，该机构将利用所分配的军人来完成其目标。”

该发言人说，受重组影响的文职人员将留在当前岗位，直至另行通知，并将接受重新分配评估。

CASI主任布伦丹·马尔瓦尼（Brendan Mulvaney）对影响的描述有所不同。他周二说，该研究所所有文职编制都将被裁撤，“实际上终结了CASI”。他说，没有军职岗位受到影响，并指出该研究所拥有两个军士长编制和一个已空缺一年多的副主任职位。

当被问及此次裁撤将如何影响该研究所的研究时，马尔瓦尼说：“所有研究一直都是由文职人员完成的。”

据马尔瓦尼称，这一决定由前任空军大学司令作出，并由空军教育与训练司令部根据在整个空军部裁减文职岗位的要求转呈。他说，该配额源自空军人力与预备役事务办公室。

马尔瓦尼说，此次裁撤“与CASI的任务无关”，而是因为该研究所不培养职业军事教育学员，而这是空军大学的主要任务。

当被问及是否有其他机构将接手CASI的中国航空航天研究时，马尔瓦尼说：“尚未确定任何机构。”他说，目前也不清楚CASI的报告、翻译和课程材料是否会继续公开提供，其网站是否会继续在线。

这些削减于周一公开，当时一份来自CASI文职人员的说明在社交媒体上流传。该员工写道，自10月1日起，CASI所有文职岗位都将失去经费，工作人员将成为“富余联邦雇员”，这是联邦人事术语，指岗位被撤销的工作人员。

该说明将CASI的未来描述为“不确定”，并补充说，“鉴于我们团队和预算规模很小，CASI发挥出了超出自身分量的作用。”

美国海军水面战军官威尔·耶尔（Will Yale）在X上发布了这份说明，他写道，美国空军部“决定关闭”CASI是“极其不幸和令人遗憾的”。他称该研究所是其领域内最知名的机构之一，并写道，它“显著增进了美国政府内外对解放军的了解”。

美国海军战争学院教授、CASI兼职研究员安德鲁·埃里克森（Andrew Erickson）指出，这一消息“仅针对CASI”。马尔瓦尼（Mulvaney）表示，此举不影响海军中国海事研究所、陆军战争学院中国陆权研究中心或海军陆战队战争学院中国作战倡议。

CASI成立于2017年，并于2021年6月15日由时任空军参谋长小查尔斯·Q·布朗（Charles Q. Brown Jr.）上将正式批准设立。该章程责成该研究所研究中国“一切会飞的东西”，称CASI是空军研究中国及其航空航天能力的首要中心。该研究所在阿拉巴马州麦克斯韦空军基地和华盛顿的麦克奈尔堡设有办公室。

根据其章程，该研究所的研究在性质上属于非机密，章程要求CASI使用公开可得的母语来源并公布研究结果。CASI翻译了解放军教材和条令，出版了参考入门读物，并开办了为期三天、无需安全许可的免费“解放军基础”课程。

CASI表示，其每两年举办一次的CASI会议于5月在国防大学举行，吸引了250多名与会者，并发布了其《解放军航空航天力量》入门读本的第五版。

据该研究所称，2025年，近8万人访问了CASI网站，下载了5万多份报告。该网站仍在运行，并于9月21日发布了一篇新论文《从愿景到警戒：北京的空间科学路线图如何构建实时杀伤网》。

一年前，CASI就已经流失了人员。在2025年10月的季度更新中，该研究所表示，国防部的一项效率推进计划裁撤了其教育主任和教育项目经理职位，原因是空军部正在“重组、撤编和调整机构”。CASI称情况“仍在变化”，一旦了解更多信息，将提供最新状态。

美国企业研究所研究员瑞安·费达修克（Ryan Fedasiuk）称此举是“分析界的毁灭性损失”，也是一个“令人无法理解的决策”。

空军表示，CASI的任务将继续，由军人接续承担马尔瓦尼（Mulvaney）所说的文职人员一直以来所做的工作。

迈克尔·斯坎伦（Michael Scanlon）是一名报道空战与太空战的国防记者。作为前美国空军 A-10 机务长，他曾为美国陆军、海军、海军陆战队和海岸警卫队的地面和海上项目提供支持。
zhParas: 10月1日，美国空军将裁撤中国航空航天研究所（China Aerospace Studies Institute）的全部10个文职岗位。该研究所是空军大学下设中心，负责发布有关中国人民解放军空中、太空和导弹力量的机密研究。该研究所所长表示，此举将实际上终止该研究所，尽管空军方面称CASI的任务仍将继续。
“作为空军教育与训练司令部正在进行的文职人员重组的一部分，将不再向中国航空航天研究所（CASI）分配文职岗位，”一名空军发言人周二在给《防务新闻》的声明中说。“CASI的任务仍在继续，该机构将利用所分配的军人来完成其目标。”
该发言人说，受重组影响的文职人员将留在当前岗位，直至另行通知，并将接受重新分配评估。
CASI主任布伦丹·马尔瓦尼（Brendan Mulvaney）对影响的描述有所不同。他周二说，该研究所所有文职编制都将被裁撤，“实际上终结了CASI”。他说，没有军职岗位受到影响，并指出该研究所拥有两个军士长编制和一个已空缺一年多的副主任职位。
当被问及此次裁撤将如何影响该研究所的研究时，马尔瓦尼说：“所有研究一直都是由文职人员完成的。”
据马尔瓦尼称，这一决定由前任空军大学司令作出，并由空军教育与训练司令部根据在整个空军部裁减文职岗位的要求转呈。他说，该配额源自空军人力与预备役事务办公室。
马尔瓦尼说，此次裁撤“与CASI的任务无关”，而是因为该研究所不培养职业军事教育学员，而这是空军大学的主要任务。
当被问及是否有其他机构将接手CASI的中国航空航天研究时，马尔瓦尼说：“尚未确定任何机构。”他说，目前也不清楚CASI的报告、翻译和课程材料是否会继续公开提供，其网站是否会继续在线。
这些削减于周一公开，当时一份来自CASI文职人员的说明在社交媒体上流传。该员工写道，自10月1日起，CASI所有文职岗位都将失去经费，工作人员将成为“富余联邦雇员”，这是联邦人事术语，指岗位被撤销的工作人员。
该说明将CASI的未来描述为“不确定”，并补充说，“鉴于我们团队和预算规模很小，CASI发挥出了超出自身分量的作用。”
美国海军水面战军官威尔·耶尔（Will Yale）在X上发布了这份说明，他写道，美国空军部“决定关闭”CASI是“极其不幸和令人遗憾的”。他称该研究所是其领域内最知名的机构之一，并写道，它“显著增进了美国政府内外对解放军的了解”。
美国海军战争学院教授、CASI兼职研究员安德鲁·埃里克森（Andrew Erickson）指出，这一消息“仅针对CASI”。马尔瓦尼（Mulvaney）表示，此举不影响海军中国海事研究所、陆军战争学院中国陆权研究中心或海军陆战队战争学院中国作战倡议。
CASI成立于2017年，并于2021年6月15日由时任空军参谋长小查尔斯·Q·布朗（Charles Q. Brown Jr.）上将正式批准设立。该章程责成该研究所研究中国“一切会飞的东西”，称CASI是空军研究中国及其航空航天能力的首要中心。该研究所在阿拉巴马州麦克斯韦空军基地和华盛顿的麦克奈尔堡设有办公室。
根据其章程，该研究所的研究在性质上属于非机密，章程要求CASI使用公开可得的母语来源并公布研究结果。CASI翻译了解放军教材和条令，出版了参考入门读物，并开办了为期三天、无需安全许可的免费“解放军基础”课程。
CASI表示，其每两年举办一次的CASI会议于5月在国防大学举行，吸引了250多名与会者，并发布了其《解放军航空航天力量》入门读本的第五版。
据该研究所称，2025年，近8万人访问了CASI网站，下载了5万多份报告。该网站仍在运行，并于9月21日发布了一篇新论文《从愿景到警戒：北京的空间科学路线图如何构建实时杀伤网》。

items.title: Department of the Air Force pilot program expands to help more military spouses
items.author: Jennifer Gonzalez
items.summary: Administered by the AFPC and AFCS, the initiative connects active-duty spouses undergoing a permanent change of station with direct hiring opportunities.
items.body:
Published Sept. 23, 2026

By Jennifer Gonzalez

Air Force Personnel Center

A professional in her own right, Kayla Amie holds a master’s degree in organizational leadership and a Bachelor of Science in education, and has worked steadily since she was legally old enough to hold a job. But when she married a U.S. Air Force Airman, that professional background no longer guaranteed a career and steady income. “Every four years you are starting from scratch. I am ok with pivoting but it’s going from the fact that you worked so hard—being a professional—and having it taken away with each move and it not being your choice,” said Amie.

Luke AFB, Arizona

Goodfellow AFB, Texas

Laughlin AFB, Texas

Mountain Home AFB, Idaho

Travis AFB, California

Patrick SFB, Florida

Ramstein AB, Ramstein-Miesenbach

RAF Croughton, Northamptonshire

RAF Mildenhall, Suffolk

RAF Lakenheath, Suffolk

RAF Feltwell, Norfolk

Kadena AB, Okinawa

Only active-duty military spouses PCSing to the listed bases currently qualify to use the pilot program. Qualified spouses can enroll at any time into the GMSC Program using the Air Force Civilian Service website here .

items.title: DM Airmen participate in Coyote Storm 26.2 to reinforce AEW 2.0 concepts
items.author: Capt. M. Anna Turpin
items.summary: The multi-day training event operationalized Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concepts across cross-functional disciplines, including field medicine, combat search and rescue, and command and control.
items.body:
Published Sept. 22, 2026

By Capt. M. Anna Turpin

355th Wing Public Affairs

Airmen from the 355th Wing strengthened their ability to operate in contested environments during Coyote Storm 26.2 at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base , Sept. 14-17. Coyote Storm 26.2 was a training exercise focused on improving flexibility and readiness through the Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concept. AEW 2.0 training requires that preparation for deployments happens long before members go into theater and ensures that they have the time to train together across disciplines.

items.summaryZh: 这场为期多天的训练活动在多个跨职能领域落实了空中远征联队2.0概念，涵盖野战医疗、战斗搜救以及指挥控制。2026年9月17日，在亚利桑那州戴维斯-蒙森空军基地，一名美国空军战斗救援军官和第48救援中队的一名伞降救援兵在“郊狼风暴26.1”演习中练习装载演练。此次训练通过简化……强化了空中远征联队2.0这一优先事项。
items.zhFull:

作者：Capt. M. Anna Turpin

第355联队公共事务办公室

9月14日至17日，第355联队的空军人员在戴维斯-蒙森空军基地举行的“郊狼风暴”26.2演习中，增强了在对抗环境中作战的能力。“郊狼风暴”26.2是一场训练演习，重点是通过“空中远征联队2.0”概念提高灵活性和战备水平。AEW 2.0训练要求，部署准备工作要远在人员进入战区之前就进行，并确保他们有时间跨专业一起训练。

items.body:
DAYTON, Ohio (AFLCMC) -- “You are part of the fight,” Lt. Gen. Jason Voorheis, commander of the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) told attendees at the Ohio Defense and Aerospace Forum earlier this week. “ General Dale White [Director, Critical Major Weapon Systems at the Pentagon] is fond of saying that militaries don't go to war - nations go to war. You all are part of what our nation brings to the fight in terms of developing fielding and getting capability into the hands of our warfighters.”

Voorheis spoke as part of a panel titled “Power Projection from the Heartland.” He was joined on stage by Brig. Gen. Timothy Helfrich, AFLCMC Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Fighters and Advanced Aircraft, alongside defense industry professionals TK Kubit and Anthony Cain. JP Nauseef of JobsOhio moderated the discussion. The forum was hosted by the Dayton Development Coalition.

Held at Wright State University on September 21, 2026, the forum highlighted the strategic alignment between Air Force modernization priorities and the Ohio defense ecosystem.

Acquisition Speed and Agility

The Ohio Defense Ecosystem

Workforce and Talent Development

In his opening remarks, Voorheis explained the Air Force acquisition workforce's shift to accept risk earlier, lean into commercial technology and open mission systems, and empower program teams to make decisions that drive projects forward.

Both Voorheis and Helfrich noted that acquisition teams at Wright-Patt and across the Center are transitioning away from platform-specific "stovepipes" to focus on broader, integrated capabilities across advanced aircraft. These teams are also balancing intensive current fleet modernization with future systems development by shifting from individual platform upgrades to an integrated, "system of systems" approach.

“I think one of the really important parts about the acquisition transformation is the change in philosophy and focus on delivering fielded capability as kind of the preeminent prioritized pacing thing that we do, and everything else is about how we achieve that to include the authorities we're giving PAEs,” noted Voorheis.

Helfrich’s Fighters and Advanced Aircraft portfolio includes the A-10, F-15, F-16, F-22, plus the FQ-42, FQ-44, other collaborative combat aircraft.

The Air Force Research Lab (AFRL) is also headquartered at Wright-Patt. Helfrich touted how AFRL led key advances in open architecture and credits AFRL with developing the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program.

“There would be no CCA without the Air Force Research Laboratory,” explained Helfrich. “Both the FQ-42 Vengeance [and] the FQ-44 Fury were heavily invested in by AFRL. Because software is sold separately with CCA, the mission autonomy work started at AFRL. They were really the ones who put together the first consortium to build Autonomous Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA). This has become a huge program, all made possible because of the investments by AFRL.”

For both Voorheis and Helfrich, the workforce and supporting infrastructure remain top concerns. Helfrich urged educators in the audience to modernize military engineering and software development classes. Both speakers noted the shortage of physical defense infrastructure in the area around Wright-Patterson, particularly for high-level classified work.

In addition to physical plant limitations, hiring remains a challenge. AFLCMC currently has over 1,700 vacancies , with more than half located at Wright-Patt. Most open positions are in technical fields like engineering and logistics. Business areas like contracting and program management also have many openings.

“We need help recruiting from the universities and from industry as well, both defense industry and non-defense industry,” explained Voorheis. “You don't have to come in with a lot of aerospace experience. What we really need is highly talented, motivated, critical thinkers.”

The panel marked the first time Lt. Gen. Voorheis has publicly spoken about his role leading AFLCMC since assuming command late last month .
items.titleZh: AFLCMC司令在俄亥俄州国防与航空航天论坛上阐述采办优先事项
items.summaryZh: 俄亥俄州代顿（AFLCMC）——“你们也是这场战斗的一部分，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）司令Lt. Gen.贾森·沃希斯（Jason Voorheis）本周早些时候在俄亥俄州国防与航空航天论坛上对与会者表示。“Gen.戴尔·怀特（五角大楼关键重大武器系统主管）喜欢说，参战的不是军队——而是国家。你们所有人都是我们国家投入这场战斗的一部分，体现在研发、列装并把能力交到我们的……手中。”
items.zhFull:
代顿，俄亥俄州（AFLCMC）——“你们是战斗的一部分，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）司令 Lt. Gen. 贾森·沃里斯（Jason Voorheis）本周早些时候在俄亥俄国防与航空航天论坛上对与会者说。“戴尔·怀特将军（Dale White）[五角大楼关键重大武器系统主管]喜欢说，军队不会开战——国家才会开战。你们所有人都是我国为这场战斗所贡献力量的一部分，无论是开发、列装，还是把能力交到我们的作战人员手中。”

沃里斯作为题为“来自腹地的力量投射”的专题讨论小组成员发言。与他同台的有 Brig. Gen. 蒂莫西·赫尔弗里希（Timothy Helfrich），AFLCMC 战斗机与先进飞机组合采办执行官（PAE），以及国防工业专业人士 TK·库比特（TK Kubit）和安东尼·凯恩（Anthony Cain）。JobsOhio 的 JP·诺西夫（JP Nauseef）主持了讨论。该论坛由代顿发展联盟主办。

论坛于2026年9月21日在莱特州立大学举行，凸显了空军现代化优先事项与俄亥俄国防生态系统之间的战略协同。

采办速度与敏捷性

俄亥俄国防生态系统

劳动力与人才发展

沃里斯在开场致辞中解释说，空军采办队伍正在转变，更早接受风险，积极采用商业技术和开放任务系统，并赋予项目团队作出推动项目前进的决策的权力。

沃里斯和赫尔弗里希都指出，Wright-Patt 以及整个中心的采办团队正从针对特定平台的“烟囱式”模式转向，专注于先进飞机更广泛的一体化能力。这些团队还在平衡当前密集的机队现代化与未来系统开发，从单个平台升级转向一体化的“系统之系统”方法。

“我认为采办转型真正重要的部分之一，是理念的转变，以及把交付已列装能力作为我们最重要的优先事项和节奏牵引，而其他一切——包括我们赋予PAE的权限——都是为了实现这一目标，”沃海斯（Voorheis）指出。

赫尔弗里希（Helfrich）的“战斗机与先进飞机”组合包括A-10、F-15、F-16、F-22，以及FQ-42、FQ-44和其他协同作战飞机。

美国空军研究实验室（AFRL）也总部设在赖特-帕特森（Wright-Patt）。赫尔弗里希盛赞AFRL在开放架构方面引领了关键进展，并将协同作战飞机（CCA）项目的发展归功于AFRL。

“没有美国空军研究实验室，就不会有CCA，”赫尔弗里希解释道。“AFRL对FQ-42‘复仇’和FQ-44‘狂怒’都投入了大量资金。由于CCA的软件是单独销售的，任务自主性工作始于AFRL。他们确实是组建首个联盟来构建自主政府参考架构（A-GRA）的一方。这已成为一个庞大的项目，而这一切都得益于AFRL的投资。”

对沃海斯和赫尔弗里希而言，劳动力和配套基础设施仍是首要关切。赫尔弗里希敦促在场教育工作者对军事工程和软件开发课程进行现代化改革。两位发言人都指出，赖特-帕特森周边地区缺乏实体国防基础设施，尤其是用于高级别机密工作的设施。

除实体设施限制外，招聘仍是一项挑战。美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）目前有超过1,700个职位空缺，其中一半以上位于赖特-帕特森。大多数空缺职位属于工程和后勤等技术领域。合同签订和项目管理等业务领域也有许多空缺。

“我们需要在从大学以及产业界招聘方面获得帮助，既包括国防产业，也包括非国防产业，”沃海斯解释道。“你不需要带着丰富的航空航天经验入职。我们真正需要的是才华出众、积极进取、善于批判性思考的人。”

此次小组讨论标志着Lt. Gen.沃海斯自上月底就任指挥官以来，首次公开谈及他领导AFLCMC的职责。

items.title: Netanyahu May Have Ignored a Dire Warning. Israel Ignores the Deeper Threat.
items.summary: Israel's strategy in Gaza is only keeping Hamas in power: deterred, but not replaced, with no real alternative given a chance. A different outcome calls for a different approach.
items.body:
Israelis are still debating whether the recent report is true—whether the United Arab Emirates warned Israel of an imminent Hamas attack roughly 10 days before the Oct. 7 massacre.

But fixating on the few days before Oct. 7 obscures a deeper flaw: The Israeli mindset, the strategic conception, remains largely unchanged. It is conflict management. Israel is using a weakened and deterred Hamas ruling Gaza as an excuse to deepen the divide between Gaza and a Palestinian Authority–run West Bank. By avoiding allowing any alternative to emerge, it is sidelining the Palestinian question altogether.

If the deadliest disaster of Jews since the Holocaust should have changed one thing, it was this. Yet, strip away the rhetoric of “total victory,” and Israel’s Gaza policy today looks quite similar, just with more bloodshed and rubble.

In recent weeks, Israeli leaders have vowed to remain in Gaza for the long term and end Hamas’s rule once and for all. Following a string of successful assassinations of Hamas commanders, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz declared: “Our message is clear: No terrorist is immune, and Hamas will not be in Gaza.”

Israel is using a weakened and deterred Hamas ruling Gaza as an excuse to deepen the divide between Gaza and a Palestinian Authority–run West Bank.

Weakening Hamas is legitimate, and so is Israel’s demand that it relinquish control of Gaza. But Israel’s revealed preference tells a different story.

Even as Israel holds an estimated 60 percent of Gaza, Hamas still controls over 95 percent of the population. Hamas is both a terrorist organization and Gaza’s de facto government; removing the former requires an alternative for the latter. Israel refused to hand that role to the Palestinian Authority but signed on to President Trump’s 20-point plan last year, which offers exactly that: a transition to the technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, eventually leading to a reformed Palestinian Authority.

The Israeli government apparently never intended to let that alternative emerge.

Members of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza remain in Cairo, with no timeline for entering Gaza. Roughly 6,000 vetted police recruits, meant to begin training months ago, have not left Gaza because Israel will not commit to letting them return.

Construction of a base for the International Stabilization Force is stalled by bureaucracy. Reconstruction of the Israeli-held “Green Zone” meant to showcase non-Hamas governance hasn’t advanced. And in the West Bank, Israeli policy is weakening the Palestinian Authority toward collapse and carving the territory into cantons to ensure no Palestinian governance, with or without Gaza, is ever viable.

Hamas has expectedly stalled the plan, too. But in August it accepted the Board of Peace’s roadmap, listing 15 principles for phased disarmament in exchange for Israel Defense Forces withdrawal. Israel has valid concerns, including the roadmap’s timeline, scope of disarmament, and Qatar and Turkey’s role in verifying compliance.

A future Israeli government that wants a different outcome will have to act like it.

But justified skepticism does not excuse refusing to engage. Instead of making Hamas back its words, Israel has effectively handed it veto power over the process, drawing international blame for stalling while Hamas gains recognition as a legitimate partner.

Domestic politics explains much of this. Israel faces a charged election on Oct. 27, and Netanyahu’s coalition cannot show compromise on Gaza. Even pressure from Trump plays in his favor, as he claims to be the only one who can stand up to who he called “the greatest friend that the state of Israel has ever had in the White House.” Netanyahu’s rivals, meantime, are trying to outflank him from the right, vowing to keep fighting rather than engage the U.S.-led plan.

But whoever wins will still have to pick up the Trump framework. The alternatives—renewed full-scale war or a Gaza permanently split between an Israeli-held east and Hamas-run west—serve neither Israel’s security interests nor produce an acceptable status quo.

Rather than campaigning on the same hawkish instinct, prime minister contenders should say that the current approach only keeps Hamas in power: deterred, but not replaced, with no real alternative given a chance.

A future Israeli government that wants a different outcome will have to act like it. This means setting a political horizon instead of managing the conflict incident by incident, taking initiative on the Trump plan and disarmament roadmap instead of being dragged along by Washington, Cairo, or Doha.

It also requires letting the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza function and supporting Palestinian Authority reform rather than treating its flaws as a pretext for exclusion and redirecting Gaza’s financial lifelines to starve Hamas economically rather than merely bombing it.

Such a shift could unlock the funding, troops, and regional cooperation the plan needs, and begin restoring Israel’s ties with Europe and the Arab world.

A new government will find it hard to change course quickly. The only way to make that happen is U.S. leadership from the top, because whoever wins will want Trump on their side.

The ceasefire, the hostages’ return, and the 20-point framework a year ago were a major achievement. The Trump administration can use this anniversary and Israel’s election to press ahead. Otherwise, Israel risks drifting back into an Oct. 6 reality: a contained, managed Hamas quietly rebuilding behind a calm facade, primed to explode again.
items.titleZh: 内塔尼亚胡（Netanyahu）或许忽视了一个严峻警告。以色列则忽视了更深层的威胁。
items.summaryZh: 以色列在加沙的战略只会让哈马斯继续掌权：受到威慑却未被取代，也没有任何真正的替代方案获得机会。要得到不同的结果，就需要不同的做法。
items.zhFull:
以色列人仍在争论，最近的那则报道是否属实——阿拉伯联合酋长国是否在10月7日屠杀发生前约10天，就警告过以色列哈马斯即将发动袭击。

但把目光死盯在10月7日之前的这几天上，会掩盖一个更深层的缺陷：以色列人的思维方式和战略构想基本没有改变，那就是冲突管理。以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。通过不让任何替代方案出现，它把巴勒斯坦问题整个边缘化了。

如果说大屠杀以来犹太人遭遇的最惨重灾难本应改变一件事，那就应该是这一点。然而，剥去“全面胜利”的说辞，以色列今天的加沙政策看上去并无二致，只是流血更多、废墟更多。

近几周，以色列领导人誓言要长期留在加沙，并彻底终结哈马斯的统治。在接连成功暗杀哈马斯指挥官之后，总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）和国防部长伊斯雷尔·卡茨（Israel Katz）宣称：“我们的信息很明确：没有哪个恐怖分子可以豁免，哈马斯不会留在加沙。”

以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。

削弱哈马斯是正当的，以色列要求其放弃对加沙的控制也是正当的。但以色列显露出的实际偏好却讲述了另一个故事。

尽管以色列控制着加沙约60%的地区，哈马斯仍控制着当地95%以上的人口。哈马斯既是恐怖组织，也是加沙事实上的政府；要铲除前者，就必须为后者提供替代方案。以色列拒绝把这一角色交给巴勒斯坦权力机构，但去年却签署了特朗普（Trump）总统的20点计划，而该计划提供的正是这一点：过渡到技术官僚性质的加沙行政管理全国委员会，最终走向改革后的巴勒斯坦权力机构。

以色列政府显然从未打算让这一替代方案出现。

加沙管理国家委员会成员仍留在开罗，没有进入加沙的时间表。大约6000名经过审查的警察新兵本应在数月前开始训练，但因以色列不愿承诺允许他们返回，至今未能离开加沙。

国际稳定部队基地的建设因官僚程序而停滞。以色列控制的“绿区”本意是展示非哈马斯治理，其重建毫无进展。在约旦河西岸，以色列的政策正削弱巴勒斯坦权力机构，使其走向崩溃，并将该地区切割成一块块飞地，以确保无论有无加沙，巴勒斯坦治理都永远无法可行。

哈马斯也不出所料地拖延了这一计划。但8月它接受了和平委员会的路线图，列出15项原则，以分阶段解除武装换取以色列国防军撤离。以色列的担忧不无道理，包括路线图的时间表、解除武装的范围，以及卡塔尔和土耳其在核查遵守情况方面的作用。

未来的以色列政府若想取得不同的结果，就必须以相应的方式行事。

但合理的怀疑并不能成为拒绝接触的借口。以色列没有迫使哈马斯兑现其言辞，反而实际上赋予其对这一进程的否决权，因拖延而招致国际指责，而哈马斯则获得合法伙伴的认可。

国内政治在很大程度上解释了这一切。以色列将于10月27日举行一场激烈的选举，内塔尼亚胡的联盟无法在加沙问题上展现妥协。就连特朗普施压也对他有利，因为他声称只有他才能顶住他所称的“以色列国在白宫有史以来最伟大的朋友”。与此同时，内塔尼亚胡的对手正试图从右翼包抄他，誓言继续战斗，而非参与美国主导的计划。

但无论谁获胜，都仍须接过特朗普的框架。其他选项——重启全面战争，或加沙永久分裂为以色列控制的东部和哈马斯控制的西部——既不符合以色列的安全利益，也无法形成可接受的现状。

总理职位角逐者不应以同样的鹰派本能进行竞选，而应指出：当前做法只会让哈马斯继续掌权——受到威慑，却未被取代，真正的替代方案从未获得机会。

未来一个想要不同结果的以色列政府，就必须以相应的方式行事。这意味着要设定政治前景，而不是逐次事件地管控冲突；要在特朗普计划和解除武装路线图上采取主动，而不是被华盛顿、开罗或多哈牵着走。

这还要求让加沙管理全国委员会能够运作，并支持巴勒斯坦权力机构改革，而不是将其缺陷当作排斥的借口，并将加沙的资金命脉转向在经济上扼杀哈马斯，而不只是对其进行轰炸。

这样的转变可能释放该计划所需的资金、部队和区域合作，并开始恢复以色列与欧洲和阿拉伯世界的关系。

新政府将很难迅速改变路线。要让这种情况发生，唯一办法是美国最高层发挥领导作用，因为无论谁获胜，都会希望特朗普站在自己一边。

一年前的停火、人质回归和20点框架是一项重大成就。特朗普政府可以利用这一周年和以色列选举来推进。否则，以色列可能重新滑回10月6日的现实：一个被遏制、被管控的哈马斯在平静表象背后悄然重建，随时准备再次爆发。

但把目光死盯在10月7日之前的这几天上，会掩盖一个更深层的缺陷：以色列人的思维方式和战略构想基本没有改变，那就是冲突管理。以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。通过不让任何替代方案出现，它把巴勒斯坦问题整个边缘化了。
如果说大屠杀以来犹太人遭遇的最惨重灾难本应改变一件事，那就应该是这一点。然而，剥去“全面胜利”的说辞，以色列今天的加沙政策看上去并无二致，只是流血更多、废墟更多。
近几周，以色列领导人誓言要长期留在加沙，并彻底终结哈马斯的统治。在接连成功暗杀哈马斯指挥官之后，总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）和国防部长伊斯雷尔·卡茨（Israel Katz）宣称：“我们的信息很明确：没有哪个恐怖分子可以豁免，哈马斯不会留在加沙。”
以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。
削弱哈马斯是正当的，以色列要求其放弃对加沙的控制也是正当的。但以色列显露出的实际偏好却讲述了另一个故事。
尽管以色列控制着加沙约60%的地区，哈马斯仍控制着当地95%以上的人口。哈马斯既是恐怖组织，也是加沙事实上的政府；要铲除前者，就必须为后者提供替代方案。以色列拒绝把这一角色交给巴勒斯坦权力机构，但去年却签署了特朗普（Trump）总统的20点计划，而该计划提供的正是这一点：过渡到技术官僚性质的加沙行政管理全国委员会，最终走向改革后的巴勒斯坦权力机构。
以色列政府显然从未打算让这一替代方案出现。
加沙管理国家委员会成员仍留在开罗，没有进入加沙的时间表。大约6000名经过审查的警察新兵本应在数月前开始训练，但因以色列不愿承诺允许他们返回，至今未能离开加沙。
国际稳定部队基地的建设因官僚程序而停滞。以色列控制的“绿区”本意是展示非哈马斯治理，其重建毫无进展。在约旦河西岸，以色列的政策正削弱巴勒斯坦权力机构，使其走向崩溃，并将该地区切割成一块块飞地，以确保无论有无加沙，巴勒斯坦治理都永远无法可行。
哈马斯也不出所料地拖延了这一计划。但8月它接受了和平委员会的路线图，列出15项原则，以分阶段解除武装换取以色列国防军撤离。以色列的担忧不无道理，包括路线图的时间表、解除武装的范围，以及卡塔尔和土耳其在核查遵守情况方面的作用。
未来的以色列政府若想取得不同的结果，就必须以相应的方式行事。
但合理的怀疑并不能成为拒绝接触的借口。以色列没有迫使哈马斯兑现其言辞，反而实际上赋予其对这一进程的否决权，因拖延而招致国际指责，而哈马斯则获得合法伙伴的认可。
国内政治在很大程度上解释了这一切。以色列将于10月27日举行一场激烈的选举，内塔尼亚胡的联盟无法在加沙问题上展现妥协。就连特朗普施压也对他有利，因为他声称只有他才能顶住他所称的“以色列国在白宫有史以来最伟大的朋友”。与此同时，内塔尼亚胡的对手正试图从右翼包抄他，誓言继续战斗，而非参与美国主导的计划。
但无论谁获胜，都仍须接过特朗普的框架。其他选项——重启全面战争，或加沙永久分裂为以色列控制的东部和哈马斯控制的西部——既不符合以色列的安全利益，也无法形成可接受的现状。
总理职位角逐者不应以同样的鹰派本能进行竞选，而应指出：当前做法只会让哈马斯继续掌权——受到威慑，却未被取代，真正的替代方案从未获得机会。
未来一个想要不同结果的以色列政府，就必须以相应的方式行事。这意味着要设定政治前景，而不是逐次事件地管控冲突；要在特朗普计划和解除武装路线图上采取主动，而不是被华盛顿、开罗或多哈牵着走。
这还要求让加沙管理全国委员会能够运作，并支持巴勒斯坦权力机构改革，而不是将其缺陷当作排斥的借口，并将加沙的资金命脉转向在经济上扼杀哈马斯，而不只是对其进行轰炸。
这样的转变可能释放该计划所需的资金、部队和区域合作，并开始恢复以色列与欧洲和阿拉伯世界的关系。
新政府将很难迅速改变路线。要让这种情况发生，唯一办法是美国最高层发挥领导作用，因为无论谁获胜，都会希望特朗普站在自己一边。
一年前的停火、人质回归和20点框架是一项重大成就。特朗普政府可以利用这一周年和以色列选举来推进。否则，以色列可能重新滑回10月6日的现实：一个被遏制、被管控的哈马斯在平静表象背后悄然重建，随时准备再次爆发。

items.title: Connecting the fight: AFA 2026 panel explores next-generation DAF battle management
items.author: Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth
items.summary: As the Department of the Air Force works to build a more connected and resilient Battle Network, military and industry leaders focused on one central challenge: how to move capability to the warfighter faster.
items.body:
Published Sept. 21, 2026

By Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth

Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs

As the Department of the Air Force works to build a more connected and resilient Battle Network , military and industry leaders focused on one central challenge: how to move capability to the warfighter faster during a panel at the Air and Space Forces Association’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference, Sept. 15.

The “Next-Generation Battle Management” panel brought together Elaine Bitonti of Collins Aerospace; retired Maj. Gen. Scott Jobe with Boeing; retired Col. Sean Lowe with SAIC; and retired Maj. Luke Savoie with Elbit America. Brig. Gen. Joshua Williams , the Department of the Air Force portfolio acquisition executive for Command, Control, Communications and Battle Management, moderated the panel.

Williams opened by emphasizing the need to move beyond systems that operate independently of one another.

“The Department of the Air Force will not accept business models built on closed software stacks, black box hardware or restricted data interfaces,” Williams said. “The government must own and govern the technical baseline to ensure rapid iterative upgrades.”

For Savoie, that openness must extend from architecture to technology operating at the edge of the fight.

“How do you solve the compute portion on the edge, so that these tools and the connected network is working further and further forward and faster and faster within the loop of the folks that are on the front edge?” Savoie asked.

Bitonti connected that challenge directly to the movement of data across the force.

“I think first, you know, we understand from a battle management perspective, it’s all about how we’re moving the data,” Bitonti said, explaining that separating software from hardware and creating flexible communications architectures can allow systems to adapt as new requirements emerge.

That flexibility, the panelists agreed, is only useful if the DAF can test and field new capabilities quickly.

“One of the keys I think for the government is rapid prototyping, demonstrations and ensuring that we have industry partnerships,” Jobe said. “In order to really prove it to the DAF Battle Network or to the Joint Force, you got to go out there and demonstrate it, show that it’s real.”

Jobe pointed to a recent example in which an AMRAAM was launched from an MQ-28 Ghost Bat and integrated with an E-7 Wedgetail and F/A-18 Hornet within nine months.

“So that’s one example of the many things we’re doing and the rapid prototyping and getting to the field to demonstrate capabilities,” Jobe said.

The panel then turned to one of the biggest barriers between development and operational use: testing, security and accreditation.

Lowe described a process where software can move through development, security compliance, developmental testing and operational testing in sequence, with each transition potentially adding weeks or months.

“This is how you get months and years of delay,” Lowe said. He pointed to an approach where developmental and operational testers work alongside developers, allowing changes to be identified and addressed much earlier. “By putting the DTOT folks in the right places, particularly with the developmental teams, we can accelerate this.”

“The ATO process is … one, it’s out of control of most of the people in program office, and when you get to it, it does bring everything to a screeching halt,” Savoie said, calling for a broader examination of cybersecurity, information technology security and accreditation processes.

Jobe similarly pointed to the security environment as an area where policy and decision-making could move faster.

“I think we could probably move a lot faster,” Jobe said. “Maybe some communication and education to the personnel that are inside the acquisition system might be beneficial.”

For Bitonti, data sharing between services and coalition partners presents another policy challenge.

“We talk about really wanting to operate as a joint force and also with our coalition partners, but there are multiple restrictions, policy restrictions on rule sets of what data we can and can’t share,” she said.

“At this point, it’s not actually a technological impediment that is causing some of our struggles sharing data. It’s policy impediments.”

As the panel closed, Williams brought the discussion back to the DAF’s responsibility to deliver capability at the pace required by an evolving fight.

“Acquisition is a warfighting function,” Williams said. “We must deliver open, resilient, software-driven capability at the speed of operational relevance.”
items.titleZh: 打通作战链路：AFA 2026专题讨论会探讨下一代DAF战斗管理
items.summaryZh: 随着空军部（DAF）致力于构建一个更加互联、更具韧性的战斗网络，军方和业界领袖聚焦于一个核心挑战：如何更快地把能力送到作战人员手中。
items.zhFull:
发布于2026年9月21日

作者：Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth

空军部长公共事务办公室

在空军部着力构建更加互联、更具韧性的“战斗网络”（Battle Network）之际，军方和业界领袖于9月15日在空军与太空军协会“空中、太空与网络大会”的一场专题讨论上，聚焦一个核心难题：如何更快地把作战能力送到作战人员手中。

“下一代战斗管理”专题讨论汇集了柯林斯航空航天公司的Elaine Bitonti、波音公司的退役Maj. Gen. Scott Jobe、SAIC公司的退役Col. Sean Lowe，以及埃尔比特美国公司的退役Maj. Luke Savoie。空军部负责指挥、控制、通信与战斗管理组合采办事务的Brig. Gen. Joshua Williams主持了讨论。

Williams在开场发言中强调，必须超越那些各自独立运行的系统。

Williams说：“空军部不会接受建立在封闭软件栈、黑箱硬件或受限数据接口之上的商业模式。政府必须拥有并管理技术基线，以确保快速迭代升级。”

在Savoie看来，这种开放性必须从体系架构延伸到在作战前沿运行的技术。

“你如何解决边缘的计算部分，从而使这些工具和互联网络在最前沿人员的循环中越来越靠前、越来越快地运行？”萨沃伊（Savoie）问道。

比通蒂（Bitonti）将这一挑战直接与部队中数据的移动联系起来。

“我认为，首先，你知道，从战斗管理角度看，我们明白关键在于我们如何移动数据，”比通蒂说，并解释称，将软件与硬件分离并创建灵活的通信架构，可以让系统在新需求出现时进行适应。

小组成员一致认为，这种灵活性只有在DAF能够快速测试和部署新能力时才有用。

“我认为，对政府而言，关键之一在于快速原型开发、演示，并确保我们拥有行业合作伙伴关系，”乔布（Jobe）说。“为了真正向DAF战斗网络或联合部队证明它，你必须走出去演示它，表明它是真实的。”

乔布指出最近的一个例子：一枚AMRAAM从一架MQ-28 Ghost Bat上发射，并在九个月内与一架E-7 Wedgetail和F/A-18 Hornet完成集成。

“因此，这只是我们所做众多事情中的一个例子，也是快速原型开发和进入实地演示能力的一个例子，”乔布说。

随后，小组转向研发与作战使用之间最大的障碍之一：测试、安全和认证。

洛(Lowe)描述了一个流程：软件会依次经过开发、安全合规、开发测试和作战测试，而每一次转段都可能增加数周或数月的时间。

“这就是为什么会出现数月乃至数年的延误，”洛(Lowe)说。他提到一种做法，即开发测试和作战测试人员与开发人员并肩工作，从而使变更能够更早被发现和解决。“把开发测试与作战测试人员放到合适的位置，尤其是与开发团队在一起，我们就能加快这一进程。”

“ATO流程……其一，它不受项目办公室大多数人的控制，而一旦进入这一环节，确实会让一切戛然而止，”萨沃伊(Savoie)说，并呼吁对网络安全、信息技术安全和认证流程进行更广泛的审视。

乔布(Jobe)同样指出，安全环境是一个政策和决策可以更快推进的领域。

“我认为我们很可能可以快得多，”乔布说。“也许对采办系统内的人员进行一些沟通和教育可能会有所裨益。”

对比通蒂(Bitonti)而言，各军种与联盟伙伴之间的数据共享构成了另一项政策挑战。

“我们谈到非常希望作为联合部队行动，也与我们的联盟伙伴共同行动，但在关于我们可以和不能共享哪些数据的规则集方面，存在多重限制，也就是政策限制，”她说。

“目前，造成我们在共享数据方面一些困难的，实际上并不是技术障碍。而是政策障碍。”

在专题讨论结束时，Williams 把讨论拉回到空军部（DAF）的职责上，即以不断演变的作战所要求的速度交付能力。

“采办是一项作战职能，”Williams 说。“我们必须以作战相关性所需的速度，交付开放、有韧性、软件驱动的能力。”

items.title: Never Underestimate the Houthis
items.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels are in a position to shape the next phase of the conflict between the United States and Iran if they attempt to renew their blockade of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. And no one should assume that a deal with Iran will bind what the Houthis do next.
items.body:
Just a few years ago, Yemen's Houthi rebels were second- or third-tier members of Iran's “Axis of Resistance,” prompting policymakers to treat them as a subsidiary of Tehran. But while they benefit from Iranian weapons, training and know-how, the Houthis also have their own interests at heart—and behave accordingly.

This armed group that controls much of northern Yemen is in position to shape the next phase of the conflict between the United States and Iran if they attempt to renew their blockade of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The Houthis could reignite the war in Yemen, scuttle efforts to make a deal with Iran and draw the United States even deeper into the region's conflicts.

A key assumption going into the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran, which began in February, was that Iran's proxy militias had been critically weakened. Hezbollah, the militant group in Lebanon that was once Iran's most powerful partner in the region, suffered heavy blows from Israel during the Gaza war, as did Hamas. Iran lost another key ally when Bashar al-Assad's regime in Syria collapsed in December 2024.

The Houthis, whose military capacity had also been weakened by U.S. strikes in 2024–25, did not jump back into the fray right away when the United States and Israel began striking Iran this year, seemingly sparing them similar blows.

Perhaps they were biding their time. Because of a quirk of geography, the Houthis are able to disrupt commercial traffic in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a choke point at the entry to the Red Sea, through which 12 percent to 15 percent of maritime trade travels. At the other end of the Red Sea lies the Suez Canal, a vital route for oil and liquefied natural gas headed to North American and European markets. With Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, the Houthis are now in an unusually powerful position.

With Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, the Houthis are now in an unusually powerful position.

They have come far in global influence since seizing Yemen's capital, Sanaa, in 2014 and expelling the internationally recognized government from the city in early 2015. When the rebel forces pushed south in March of that year, in an attempt to take over territory in southern Yemen, a coalition led by Saudi Arabia and backed by the United States intervened.

The once localized war became a regional conflict and a devastating humanitarian crisis. Finally, facing a stalemate and significant international pressure, both sides agreed to a U.N.-brokered cease-fire in April 2022. By that point, the Houthis had created a de facto state in northern Yemen, while the weak Saudi-backed government nominally ruled parts of the south and west.

The Houthis flexed their muscles by attacking shipping vessels in the Red Sea early in the Israel-Gaza war that started in 2023. Using low-cost, low-tech equipment like one-way attack drones, missiles and unmanned surface vessels, the Houthis made the crossing more dangerous, driving up the cost of insuring commercial ships as much as twentyfold, effectively closing the strait. The only alternate route forced ships around the southern tip of the African continent, an extra 4,000 or more nautical miles, increasing shipping costs.

Last month, the Houthis resumed attacks on Red Sea shipping, striking Saudi-linked commercial oil tankers and hitting Saudi energy and transportation infrastructure. They were responding to what they claimed were Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa Airport's runway on July 13, seemingly in an effort to prevent an incoming Iranian flight from landing. For now, commercial ships continue to transit the Red Sea, although tanker traffic has declined substantially over the past month. Houthi attacks have also continued on ships the group claims are Saudi-aligned, and an attack on a cargo ship on Aug. 12 included the first reported fatalities of this latest round of attacks.

In recent days, the Houthis have claimed attacks on a ship in the Red Sea port of Mokha, which is held by forces allied with the internationally recognized government of Yemen, and on airports and oil refinery infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

With the effective closure of Hormuz, the Red Sea-Suez route has become even more important. Most notably, Saudi Arabia had sought to avoid Hormuz by routing crude oil via a pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu on its western coast. The new Houthi attacks have disrupted that option. The near closure of both Hormuz and the Suez routes could compound problems for global trade, pushing the cost of oil and inflation even higher.

Now the Houthis are positioned to step up their involvement in an already raging regional conflagration, complicating efforts to end it. Some may assume that this move is at the behest of Iran, but the reality is likely more complicated.

Highly attuned to their own interests and pragmatic in the international arena, the Houthis have proved savvy at choosing when to enter or escalate conflicts. When they attacked shipping in the Red Sea in 2023–25, for example, they said it was to pressure Israel to de-escalate its operations in Gaza. The strikes also bolstered their legitimacy in the territory they control in northern Yemen, diverting attention from their governance failures at a time when their popularity had eroded.

The Houthis have proved savvy at choosing when to enter or escalate conflicts.

This time, the Houthis appear to see an opening to gain leverage in negotiations with Saudi Arabia to reach a political settlement in the Yemeni war—or an opportunity to resume attacks against the internationally backed government.

The previous round of Houthi attacks, in 2023–25, had a significant but ultimately manageable effect on the global economy. Estimates suggested that the ensuing shipping disruptions would have a small impact on inflation. The economic effects of closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the same time as Hormuz are likely to be more dire.

While the United States looks to wind down the war with Iran, the Houthis are threatening to resume their war in Yemen, which would likely draw in Saudi Arabia, menace the global oil trade and keep the region unstable.

It will be difficult to de-escalate regional tensions without addressing the Houthis' threat directly, rather than assuming it can be resolved by dealing with their supposed boss, Iran. At the same time, no one should assume that a deal with Iran will bind what the Houthis do next. The international community should confront them as a pragmatic and dangerous actor making decisions in their own self-interest.
items.titleZh: 永远不要低估胡塞武装
items.summaryZh: 如果也门胡塞武装试图重启对曼德海峡的封锁，他们就有能力塑造美国与伊朗之间冲突的下一阶段走向。而且任何人都不应以为与伊朗达成协议就能约束胡塞武装接下来的行动。
items.zhFull:
就在几年前，也门胡塞叛军还只是伊朗“抵抗轴心”中的二线或三线成员，这促使政策制定者将其视为德黑兰的附属。然而，尽管他们受益于伊朗的武器、训练和技术，胡塞武装也有自己的利益考量，并据此行事。

这支控制也门北部大片地区的武装组织，如果试图重启对曼德海峡的封锁，就有能力影响美国与伊朗冲突的下一阶段。胡塞武装可能重新点燃也门战争，破坏与伊朗达成协议的努力，并把美国进一步拖入该地区的冲突。

在2月开始的美以对伊朗袭击中，一个关键假设是伊朗的代理民兵已遭到严重削弱。黎巴嫩激进组织真主党曾是伊朗在该地区最强大的伙伴，在加沙战争期间遭到以色列重创，哈马斯也是如此。2024年12月，叙利亚巴沙尔·阿萨德 (Bashar al-Assad) 政权垮台，伊朗又失去一个关键盟友。

胡塞武装的军事能力也曾因美国在2024—25年的打击而遭到削弱；当美国和以色列今年开始打击伊朗时，他们并未立即重新加入战团，似乎因此免遭类似打击。

也许他们是在等待时机。由于地理上的特殊条件，胡塞武装能够扰乱曼德海峡的商业航运；这条海峡是红海入口处的咽喉要道，12%至15%的海上贸易经此通行。红海另一端是苏伊士运河，这是石油和液化天然气运往北美和欧洲市场的重要通道。随着伊朗实际上封锁霍尔木兹海峡，胡塞武装如今处于异常强大的地位。

随着伊朗实际上封锁霍尔木兹海峡，胡塞武装如今处于异常强大的地位。

自2014年夺取也门首都萨那，并于2015年初将国际公认的政府赶出该市以来，他们在全球影响力方面已取得长足进展。当年3月，叛军向南推进，试图夺取也门南部领土，沙特阿拉伯领导、美国支持的联军随即介入。

这场一度局部化的战争演变为地区冲突和毁灭性的人道主义危机。最终，面对僵局和巨大的国际压力，双方于2022年4月同意接受联合国斡旋的停火。到那时，胡塞武装已在也门北部建立了一个事实上的国家，而沙特支持的软弱政府名义上统治着南部和西部的部分地区。

胡塞武装在2023年爆发的以色列-加沙战争初期通过袭击红海航运船只来展示实力。他们使用单向攻击无人机、导弹和无人水面艇等低成本、低技术装备，使这一航道穿越变得更加危险，将商船保险费率推高至原来的二十倍之多，实际上封锁了该海峡。唯一的替代航线迫使船只绕行非洲大陆南端，额外航行4,000 nautical miles以上，推高了航运成本。

上个月，胡塞武装恢复对红海航运的袭击，打击与沙特有关联的商用油轮，并袭击沙特的能源和交通基础设施。他们称此举是对沙特7月13日空袭萨那机场跑道的回应，后者似乎意在阻止一架即将抵达的伊朗航班降落。目前，商船仍在继续穿行红海，尽管过去一个月油轮运输量大幅下降。胡塞武装还继续袭击其声称与沙特结盟的船只，而8月12日对一艘货船的袭击中出现了本轮袭击中首批报告的死亡事件。

近日，胡塞武装声称袭击了红海摩卡港的一艘船只——该港由与也门国际公认政府结盟的武装力量控制——以及沙特阿拉伯的机场和炼油厂基础设施。

随着霍尔木兹海峡实际关闭，红海—苏伊士航线变得更加重要。最突出的是，沙特阿拉伯曾试图通过管道将原油输送至其西海岸的延布港，以避开霍尔木兹海峡。胡塞武装的新一轮袭击使这一选择受阻。霍尔木兹海峡和红海—苏伊士航线近乎同时关闭，可能使全球贸易问题雪上加霜，进一步推高油价和通胀。

如今，胡塞武装已有条件加大介入这场本已熊熊燃烧的地区冲突，使结束冲突的努力更加复杂。一些人可能认为此举是应伊朗指使，但实际情况可能更为复杂。

胡塞武装高度关注自身利益，在国际舞台上行事务实，在何时介入或升级冲突的问题上表现出精明的判断力。例如，在2023—2025年袭击红海航运时，他们称此举是为了向以色列施压，促使其缓和在加沙的军事行动。这些袭击还增强了其在也门北部所控制地区的合法性，在其支持率下滑之际转移了人们对其治理失败的注意力。

胡塞武装在何时介入或升级冲突的问题上表现得相当精明。

这一次，胡塞武装似乎看到了在与沙特阿拉伯谈判中获取筹码、推动也门战争政治解决的机会——或者是恢复对国际社会支持的政府发动袭击的契机。

上一轮胡塞武装袭击（2023—2025年）对全球经济造成了显著但最终尚可消化的影响。当时的评估认为，随之而来的航运中断对通胀的影响有限。而一旦曼德海峡与霍尔木兹海峡同时被封锁，其经济后果可能更为严峻。

在美国寻求结束与伊朗的战争之际，胡塞武装却威胁要在也门重启战事，这很可能把沙特阿拉伯卷入其中，威胁全球石油贸易，并使该地区持续动荡不安。

如果不直接应对胡塞武装的威胁，而是想当然地认为通过与其所谓的后台伊朗打交道就能解决问题，那么缓和地区紧张局势将十分困难。与此同时，任何人都不应以为与伊朗达成协议就能约束胡塞武装接下来的行动。国际社会应当把他们视为一个务实而危险、依据自身利益行事的行动方来加以应对。
